prs.title: fix(server): allow JSON Accept in JSON response mode
prs.author: Genmin
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs fix the same bug in webStandardStreamableHttp.ts: the Accept header validation for Streamable HTTP JSON response mode currently rejects requests unless the header lists BOTH application/json and text/event-stream, even though a client using JSON-only response mode has no reason to advertise event-stream support. prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs fix the same bug in webStandardStreamableHttp.ts: the Accept header validation for Streamable HTTP JSON response mode currently rejects requests unless the header lists BOTH application/json and text/event-stream, even though a client using JSON-only response mode has no reason to advertise event-stream support. Both PRs relax this check to accept a JSON-only Accept header, touching the exact same validation block (lines ~598-614). (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #1996 adds a dedicated acceptsMediaType() parser that correctly handles Accept header semantics per RFC 7231: it splits on media-range parameters, discards entries with q=0 (explicitly rejected types), and honors wildcards (type/* and */*). #2046 instead does a bare acceptHeader.includes('application/json') / includes('text/event-stream') substring check, which has two correctness gaps #1996 avoids: (1) it will false-positive on any substring match (e.g. an Accept value containing 'application/json-patch+json' or 'application/vnd.api+json' would incorrectly count as accepting plain JSON), and (2) it ignores q=0, so a client that explicitly disqualifies JSON (e.g. 'application/json;q=0') would still be treated as accepting it. #1996 is also structured as a reusable helper rather than inline string checks, making it easier to extend/test.

clusters.pick_reason: #1996 adds a dedicated acceptsMediaType() parser that correctly handles Accept header semantics per RFC 7231: it splits on media-range parameters, discards entries with q=0 (explicitly rejected types), and honors wildcards (type/* and */*). #2046 instead does a bare acceptHeader.includes('application/json') / includes('text/event-stream') substring check, which has two correctness gaps #1996 avoids: (1) it will false-positive on any substring match (e.g. an Accept value containing 'application/json-patch+json' or 'application/vnd.api+json' would incorrectly count as accepting plain JSON), and (2) it ignores q=0, so a client that explicitly disqualifies JSON (e.g. 'application/json;q=0') would still be treated as accepting it. #1996 is also structured as a reusable helper rather than inline string checks, making it easier to extend/test.

clusters.pick_reason: #1996 adds a dedicated acceptsMediaType() parser that correctly handles Accept header semantics per RFC 7231: it splits on media-range parameters, discards entries with q=0 (explicitly rejected types), and honors wildcards (type/* and */*). #2046 instead does a bare acceptHeader.includes('application/json') / includes('text/event-stream') substring check, which has two correctness gaps #1996 avoids: (1) it will false-positive on any substring match (e.g. an Accept value containing 'application/json-patch+json' or 'application/vnd.api+json' would incorrectly count as accepting plain JSON), and (2) it ignores q=0, so a client that explicitly disqualifies JSON (e.g. 'application/json;q=0') would still be treated as accepting it. #1996 is also structured as a reusable helper rather than inline string checks, making it easier to extend/test.

members.author: Genmin
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs fix the same bug in webStandardStreamableHttp.ts: the Accept header validation for Streamable HTTP JSON response mode currently rejects requests unless the header lists BOTH application/json and text/event-stream, even though a client using JSON-only response mode has no reason to advertise event-stream support. clusters.pick_reason: #2215 fixes an additional real behavioral bug beyond the trailing-slash regex: shouldAttemptFallback still compared pathname === '/' even though normalization always reduces a root path to '', causing a redundant extra discovery fetch on root-like paths — #2214 only touches the slash-stripping and leaves that inconsistency in place. #2215 also extracts the fix into a shared normalizeDiscoveryPath() helper rather than inlining the regex twice, reducing duplicated logic across call sites.

members.title: chore(client): normalize trailing slashes in discovery paths
members.author: raashish1601
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2215: Both PRs fix the same root cause: buildWellKnownPath's trailing-slash stripping used `pathname.endsWith('/') ? slice(0,-1)` which only removes one trailing slash and leaves the root-path ('/' -> '') case inconsistent with the '/' check used elsewhere in the discovery flow, producing malformed double-slash well-known URLs (e.g. '/foo//.well-known/...'). Both PRs replace this with the same `pathname.replace(/\/+$/, '')` regex in the identical buildWellKnownPath hunk (same line range ~1035-1038), so they are guaranteed to merge-conflict on the exact same code.
